body:
Evan Zhao: FYI we just got an urgent escalation from AcmePayments. After the model rollout yesterday their codegen output started producing code that doesn't compile. Customer says this blocks a release. Ticket #CS-12345.

Evan Zhao: Summary from customer: prompt that previously produced a working TypeScript class now emits missing imports, wrong method signatures, and sometimes omits await on async calls — leading to TypeScript compile errors. They said behavior changed exactly after the `redwood-codegen-3.3-quant` rollout.

Evan Zhao: Repro steps (from customer):
1) Send the prompt below to our /v1/generate endpoint with model=redwood-codegen-3.3-quant
2) Run `tsc` on the produced file

Prompt (customer):
```
// Generate a TypeScript class for interacting with the Payments API
// Include methods: createCharge(amount:number): Promise<string>, refundCharge(id:string): Promise<boolean>
// Use axios, include proper imports and error handling
```

Customer output (example):
```
class PaymentsClient {
  async createCharge(amount:number) {
    // missing axios import and missing 'await'
    const resp = axios.post('/charges', {amount})
    return resp.data.id
  }
}

// compile error: 'axios' is not defined; also missing method refundCharge
```

Evan Zhao: Expected output: complete class with imports, both methods, proper async/await and typed return values. They attached a commit showing earlier model (redwood-codegen-3.2) output that compiled fine.

Jin Park: @Evan thanks for the summary — tagging eng. Do we have a deploy log that matches their reported time window? They said rollout happened ~2026-03-04 09:30 UTC.

runtime-bot: deploy notification: model-profile(redwood-codegen-3.3-quant) promoted to Default pool at 2026-03-04T09:28:14Z by release-ci (build 3.3.12).

Priya Singh: @Jin @Evan I can take this. Can you paste the exact API request body and headers the customer used? Want to reproduce locally pinned to their model. Also, any prompt templates or system messages?

Evan Zhao: they sent this curl (redacted API key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-codegen-3.3-quant","prompt":"// Generate a TypeScript class for interacting with the Payments API\n// Include methods: createCharge(amount:number): Promise<string>, refundCharge(id:string): Promise<boolean>\n// Use axios, include proper imports and error handling\n","max_tokens":512}'
```

Evan Zhao: customer also included that when they pinned `redwood-codegen-3.2` everything compiled again. They attached side-by-side diffs.

Priya Singh: OK reproducing now with pinned 3.3-quant. If I see the same regression, we'll need rollback policy or hotfix for codegen heuristics. I'll post logs.

(Minutes later)

Priya Singh: Reproduced. Output matches customer's broken snippet. Looks like the model is omitting imports and occasionally dropping method stubs when prompts are short. Suspect a change in completion distribution from the quantized runtime — maybe truncation/prefix handling or a special token mis-emitted that confuses the generation boundary.

Priya Singh: Quick mitigation options:
- Ask customer to include a longer system/instruction priming (workaround)
- Pin them to redwood-codegen-3.2 (available)
- Rollback redwood-codegen-3.3-quant from default pool until we patch

Maya Chen: Customer is blocked on their release. They want rollback if we can't guarantee a quick fix. SLA impact: P2. Customer threatens to pause on Dedicated contract if this persists.

Marco Alvarez: @Priya can you share request/response traces so we can check if network truncation or response streaming cut the document? Also need per-request latency and chunking metadata. Please attach trace IDs.

Priya Singh: Trace IDs (sample): rtx-20260304-09-31-az1-7a3f, rtx-20260304-09-32-ff1d. Responses show full content length on our edge but tokenization step in the runtime produced unexpected end-of-sequence tokens earlier than before.

Priya Singh: Here's a representative response body I captured (trimmed):
```
{
  "id":"gen_abc123",
  "model":"redwood-codegen-3.3-quant",
  "text":"import {\nclass PaymentsClient {\n  async createCharge(amount:number) {\n    const resp = axios.post('/charges', {amount})\n    return resp.data.id\n  }\n}\n",
  "tokens": [ ... , "import", "{", "class", "PaymentsClient", ... , "axios", ",", "post", "'", "/charges", "'", "}"
}
```

Priya Singh: Note token stream contains 'import' token but the model doesn't produce the complete import statement — suggests the model may be emitting separated tokens that our detokenizer doesn't stitch into valid syntax after quantization. Could be a vocab mapping/regression with the quantized tokenizer/kernel.

Marco Alvarez: We'll pull kernel logs and tokenizer diffs for build 3.3.12. Assigning to eng-runtime. @oncall-runtime can you prioritize?

oncall-runtime: Acknowledged. Putting high priority. Will start a canary rollback if we confirm regression across >5 customers.

Maya Chen: Customer wants immediate pin. Jin can you send them instructions for pinning model via appendix in support ticket? Also offer temporary mitigation: add import stub to their prompt until we resolve.

Jin Park: On it — sending pin instructions and workaround. Also asked for a minimal failing example repo. Customer responded with a tiny gist: https://gist.github.com/acmepayments/bad-codegen-example

Priya Singh: Next steps for eng:
1) Validate tokenizer output differences between 3.2 and 3.3-quant on the exact prompt corpus.
2) Run tokenization/detokenization round-trip tests for code tokens (imports, punctuation, async/await patterns).
3) If confirmed, rollback 3.3-quant from Default pool and rerun CI with quant kernel fixes.

Priya Singh: For product/ops: we should add an automated smoke test for compileability for TypeScript/Go codegen prompts during rollout gating. This would have caught this. Filing follow-up: PROD-584.

Maya Chen: Customer update sent: we've pinned their account to 3.2 and provided workaround. They're relieved but want timeline. I told them eng is investigating and we'll update within 24 hours.

Priya Singh: I have a failing unit test example and a small script to reproduce locally:
```
# reproduce.sh
python reproduce.py --model redwood-codegen-3.3-quant --prompt-file bad_prompt.txt
# then run tsc on output
```

Priya Singh: Attaching reproducer to ENG ticket: ENG-9012. If anyone wants to debug tokenizer tables I'm in the runtime-debug channel.

Marco Alvarez: Collected kernel logs show a token id remapping in quantized tokenizer table at index 16532 — correlates with '[' and '{' tokens in some builds. Suspecting an off-by-one in the quant table generation.

Priya Singh: Thanks Marco. If that's confirmed we'll prepare a quick patch to regenerates quant tables and run a canary. If rollback is necessary, please coordinate with release and notify customers.

runtime-bot: rollback action queued: canary rollback for model redwood-codegen-3.3-quant initiated by oncall-runtime at 2026-03-04T13:12:03Z.

Evan Zhao: Closing loop: customer pinned and working for now. Eng/Runtime to follow up in ENG-9012 and PROD-584. I'll keep CS-12345 updated.

Priya Singh: Leaving notes here for auditors: include side-by-side token streams, the failing TS compile output, and kernel quant table diffs. We'll aim to have a hotfix within 24–48 hours.

Maya Chen: Thanks all. If we need legal/comms escalation, I'll post in #marketing.

Jin Park: Marking thread as ongoing — will update CS ticket once rollback completes or we have a root cause. :thumbsup:
